analysis.investment_thesis: Crizac is a textbook fast grower — a B2B intermediary connecting Indian students to foreign universities with a 64% net profit CAGR and zero debt, yet trading at a P/E of only 20.8x. Even assuming growth decelerates sharply to 30% forward, the PEG sits near 0.65 — that's the kind of number that gets me excited.
key_strengths: Exceptional unit economics: ROE 36%, ROCE 48%, zero debt — this is an asset-light toll-booth on Indian outbound education
PEG ratio ~0.65 using conservative 30% forward growth — deeply undervalued for the growth rate on offer
Four-year revenue CAGR of 66% with expanding operating margins (21%+) — the story keeps getting better, not worse
key_risks: Regulatory risk: UK and Canada have been tightening student visa policies since 2023 — this company's revenue lives and dies by destination-country immigration rules
Other income (INR 35–53 Cr/yr) represents ~25–35% of net profit — if this is mark-to-market investments rather than operations, reported earnings quality is overstated
High promoter holding at 79.94% leaves minimal float for institutional buying and creates governance concentration risk
red_flags: Other income of INR 35 Cr in FY25 against net profit of INR 153 Cr — core operating profits may be weaker than headline numbers suggest
Investing cash outflows of INR 149 Cr in FY25 with capex of only INR 1 Cr — bulk appears to be financial investments, not business reinvestment; source and nature need scrutiny
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crizac is what I call a classic fast grower hiding in plain sight — a Kolkata-based education consultancy that earns fees from UK/Canada/Australia/NZ universities for recruiting Indian students. Revenue has compounded at 66% for four years (INR 111 Cr → INR 849 Cr), net profits at 64% (INR 21 Cr → INR 153 Cr), and the balance sheet is spotless: zero borrowings, INR 89 Cr cash, INR 565 Cr reserves. At P/E 20.8x on a company growing this fast, the PEG is under 0.7 even if I slash the historical growth rate by more than half. The forward P/E of 16x tells me the market is pricing in earnings acceleration — and so far management has earned that trust.

The one thing that gives me pause is the "Other Income" line — INR 45–53 Cr in FY23–24 against net profits of INR 112–116 Cr means core operating earnings were effectively propped up by ~40% from non-operating sources. FY25 improved (other income INR 35 Cr, net profit INR 153 Cr), but I'd want to know exactly what's generating that income. The bigger structural risk is external: Canada slashed study permit approvals in 2024 and the UK raised financial requirements for students. If destination-country policies tighten further, Crizac's recruitment volumes could stall regardless of how well management executes. For now, the growth, the balance sheet, and the price are all in my favor — I'd call this a buy with a watchful eye on visa policy headlines.
